name: Nothing gathered
description: The session starts with the goal alone; a helper searches the files for the request's words on its own (the session as it was).
advantages: Free; nothing to configure; nothing can be wrong.
disadvantages: Never uses the notes the person saved; a request with no distinctive word ("my practice") is answered from whatever files share a word.

name: Notes found by the request's words
description: Ranks every note by how often the request's words occur in it, the focus and the scope ignored: what a helper finds when it searches for the word.
advantages: Free; finds a note that names the thing asked about.
disadvantages: Picks lookalike notes from other homes, misses a request with no shared word, and shows notes outside the person's scope.

name: The configured focus first
description: The notes of the person's configured sources through the Context Retriever's focus_first arm: the named focus ranked first (soft affinity), the scope fence kept, the focus's overview always offered, the newest notes of the focus added when the request touches it; then the brief with the rule to use them before searching, and the one line.
advantages: Free and local; reads the person's own notes before any search; the scope fence holds; a request about something else gets only the short overview.
disadvantages: Its limits are fixed by reading and tuned on invented cases; a request whose words match nothing in the focus gets only the overview; a stray shared word ("checks" and "check") brings a note along. The word-count floor is a word match used as the gate for relevance: it cannot find a note that bears on a request without sharing two of its words, and was rejected as the design for what reaches the mind; kept as the baseline.

name: Candidates ranked by words, relevance judged by the fast tier
description: The configured focus first, made generous (no word-count floor: every note that matches at all, the focus's notes first, then the overview and the newest), only proposes candidates. A fast-tier model judges them top down in pages of five: two independent views (does the answer need it, is the request about it) run in parallel and a note is kept only when both name it; the next page is reviewed only while the page just reviewed held a relevant note, so a request nothing bears on costs one page. Only judged notes reach the brief; with no model, an error or a timeout nothing is added and the failure is logged.
advantages: A trivial or unrelated request gets nothing and costs one small call pair; a note that shares no word with the request can still be found when it bears on it (standing guidance); no word count is ever the gate.
disadvantages: Paid (two fast-tier calls per page); slower than the free arm; a note the ranking puts after an empty page is never reached; with no model it adds nothing.
